key_insight: Embedding an asymptotic boundary-layer corrector in a neural solver maintains accuracy as viscosity decreases, without requiring a grid that resolves the thin vorticity layer.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce training costs for low-viscosity flow solvers by representing wall layers analytically rather than resolving them numerically.
method: Use a singular-layer PINN for the 2D incompressible vorticity–stream function equations with slip boundary conditions.
Tie the asymptotic corrector amplitude to the network’s wall trace, avoiding prior knowledge of the limiting solution.
Build an sl-FVNN using coarse-grid finite-volume flux differences for the residual Laplacian.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports viscosity-uniform errors over six decades for Stokes and Navier–Stokes tests, with sl-FVNN matching sl-PINN accuracy within random-seed scatter at about half the training-step cost.
watch_item: Results concern 2D flows with slip boundary conditions; applicability to no-slip walls, complex geometries, or 3D flows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Singular layer neural networks for the Navier-Stokes equations at small viscosity
